text:
Juraj Slafkovský has no goals in nine games, on 2.7 expected goals, and only two all season on 6.1 expected. That's one of the bigger finishing gaps in the league, the sort that tends to close. He's still contributing (ten assists, including feeds for Nick Suzuki), but a 30-goal scorer from last season should be scoring.

The Athletic wrote after Montreal's win over Utah that the version of Slafkovský they saw needs to be the one that shows up every night. That's the right framing. Montreal is about even in chances at five on five with him on, and Evolving-Hockey had opponents' chances rising with him on last season (bottom 7% of forwards), while he faced top competition.

He's 22, a first overall pick with 300 games behind him. His ice time has dipped almost two minutes a night lately. Our range has him at 14 to 28 goals for the season, with the bounce-back built in.
